title: String Quartet in E-flat major, Op. 33 No. 2, “The Joke”
hook: A quartet whose last page keeps stopping, so that nobody in the room can tell when it is over.

painting.title: Soap Bubbles
painting.pairingNote: A young man blows a bubble while a small boy watches over the ledge, waiting for the moment it bursts; Haydn’s finale plays the same game of held breath with its silences.

facts: Haydn wrote the six quartets of Op. 33 in 1781, ten years after his last set. He offered copies to subscribers in December 1781, saying they were written “in a completely new and special way”. They are lighter and more conversational than his earlier quartets, and in each the minuet is replaced by a [[scherzo|scherzo]], Italian for “joke”.

At least one of them was played on Christmas Day 1781 in the Vienna apartment of the visiting Grand Duke Paul of Russia, later Tsar Paul I. Haydn dedicated the set to him, which is why they are known as the “Russian” quartets. They were printed by Artaria in Vienna in 1782.

The English nickname “The Joke” came later. It refers to the end of the finale, where the music breaks into pieces separated by longer and longer silences. A story says Haydn wrote it to win a bet that the ladies in the audience would start talking before the music stopped; it is told as a story, without evidence.
The set is often said to have spurred Mozart, newly settled in Vienna, to write his own six quartets, which he dedicated to Haydn in 1785.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a friendly conversation built from one phrase (I), a stamping peasant dance with a sliding village fiddler (II), a solemn song that begins in the low voices (III), a quick dance that cannot decide when to end (IV).

movements.heading: Allegro moderato, cantabile
movements.summary: The first violin sings a friendly, easy-going tune over soft, pulsing chords, and almost everything in the movement grows out of its opening phrase. It is a [[sonata-form|sonata form]] in which the four players keep passing the phrase between them, like people in conversation.

mainIdeas.name: The opening phrase
mainIdeas.description: a short, smiling tune in the first violin, starting with a little upbeat.

mainIdeas.name: The repeated notes
mainIdeas.description: a passage where all four instruments churn out quick repeated notes, sounding for a moment like a whole orchestra.

stops.hear: The first violin sings a smooth, cheerful tune over quietly pulsing chords in the other three
stops.happening: The opening phrase, the seed of the whole movement

stops.hear: Quicker notes lead the music away from home; the first violin climbs
stops.happening: The music moves to a new key, B-flat major

stops.hear: Short phrases tossed between the instruments with little gaps, then all four play fast repeated notes together
stops.happening: The end of the [[exposition|exposition]]: four players imitating an orchestra

stops.hear: The opening tune again, from the start
stops.happening: The exposition is repeated

stops.hear: The first bar of the tune is passed from instrument to instrument, overlapping, in new keys
stops.happening: The [[development|development]] begins

stops.hear: Rushing figures in the first violin, in darker minor keys
stops.happening: The tensest part of the development

stops.hear: The opening tune comes back, at home in E-flat
stops.happening: The [[recapitulation|recapitulation]]

stops.hear: The development begins again
stops.happening: The second half is repeated

stops.label: Last 15 seconds
stops.hear: A quiet close on a fragment of the opening phrase
stops.happening: The movement ends as it began

notice: Count how often you hear the first three or four notes of the opening tune. They turn up in every instrument, in nearly every corner of the movement.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: The Doric Quartet plays both halves of the movement twice, which is why it lasts almost nine minutes; versions without the second repeat take five or six.

movements.heading: Scherzo: Allegro
movements.summary: Not a courtly minuet but a country dance: heavy repeated chords for stamping feet, and a few cheeky surprises in the phrasing. In the middle section, the [[trio|trio]], the first violin plays like a village fiddler, sliding from note to note.

mainIdeas.name: The dance
mainIdeas.description: a sturdy, stamping tune in three beats, with thick, repeated chords.

mainIdeas.name: The trio
mainIdeas.description: the first violin’s tune with slides, over a steady chug in the second violin and long held notes below.

stops.hear: A sturdy dance with heavy, stamping chords; after a few bars the two violins slip in a short, sly phrase that breaks the regular pattern
stops.happening: The [[scherzo|scherzo]], an Austrian peasant dance

stops.hear: The second part: the dance wanders, with grumbling half-steps in the violins
stops.happening: The second half of the scherzo, then its repeat

stops.hear: Lighter and more rustic: the first violin slides between notes, over a busy second violin and long, droning notes in viola and cello
stops.happening: The [[trio|trio]]. Haydn marked the slides by asking for the same finger on neighbouring notes

stops.hear: The stamping dance returns
stops.happening: The scherzo again, played straight through

stops.label: Last 10 seconds
stops.hear: Two firm chords
stops.happening: The end

notice: In the trio, listen to the first violin’s slides. Haydn wanted them; 19th-century editors found them vulgar and took them out of their editions.

movements.heading: Largo e sostenuto
movements.summary: A slow, solemn song. It begins, for the first time in Haydn’s quartets, with only the viola and cello, the two lowest instruments; the violins then sing the same melody. Gentle song and forceful outbursts take turns, and each time the melody returns it is dressed in a richer texture.

mainIdeas.name: The melody
mainIdeas.description: a broad, hymn-like tune, first in the low voices.

mainIdeas.name: The outbursts
mainIdeas.description: short, forceful chords with silences between them.

stops.hear: Only viola and cello: a slow, grave duet
stops.happening: The melody in the two lowest instruments

stops.hear: The two violins sing the same melody, higher; the cello adds soft, murmuring notes
stops.happening: The violins take over

stops.hear: Suddenly forceful: short chords with silences between them
stops.happening: The first outburst

stops.hear: The melody returns in the second violin, while the first violin murmurs quick notes above it; the cello is silent
stops.happening: First return of the melody, now in three parts

stops.hear: The forceful chords again
stops.happening: A second outburst

stops.hear: The melody in the first violin, with the viola murmuring quick notes beneath; all four play
stops.happening: Second return, in full four-part sound

stops.label: Last 30 seconds
stops.hear: Soft, sighing figures, and a quiet close
stops.happening: The end of the movement

notice: Follow the melody each time it comes back: low voices only, then three instruments, then all four. The tune hardly changes; its setting grows.

movements.heading: Finale: Presto
movements.summary: A quick, bubbly [[rondo|rondo]] in a lilting six-time: a catchy refrain that keeps returning between contrasting sections. At the end Haydn stops everything for a few slow bars, then brings back the refrain broken into two-bar pieces, with longer and longer silences between them, until no one can tell whether it is over.

mainIdeas.name: The refrain
mainIdeas.description: a light, skipping tune made of short two-bar phrases.

mainIdeas.name: The broken ending
mainIdeas.description: the same phrases, separated by silence.

stops.hear: The first violin skips through a quick, cheerful tune in short phrases
stops.happening: The refrain, each half played twice

stops.hear: The tune gives way to a new idea that wanders into a darker key
stops.happening: The first contrasting section

stops.hear: The cheerful tune again
stops.happening: The refrain returns

stops.hear: A new section: the first violin repeats a high note again and again, then broad, important-sounding runs; then short phrases stop and start
stops.happening: The second contrasting section, ending in hesitations

stops.hear: The tune once more
stops.happening: The last refrain

stops.hear: A pause; then four slow, solemn bars
stops.happening: A short Adagio, as if the piece were winding up seriously

stops.hear: The tune returns at full speed, but in two-bar fragments with silences between them that grow longer each time
stops.happening: The joke

stops.label: Last 20 seconds
stops.hear: After the longest silence, the first two bars of the tune, quietly, and nothing more
stops.happening: The quartet ends on the opening of its tune

notice: During the silences at the end, notice yourself waiting. That uncertainty is the point of the joke: the music ends on a beginning.

threads.title: Conversation
threads.body: In all four movements the tune travels: the first movement’s phrase is passed around, the slow movement starts in the low voices, and the trio gives the first violin a solo turn as a village fiddler.

threads.title: Jokes
threads.body: A minuet turned into a peasant dance, slides that later editors removed, and an ending that keeps the listener guessing. Haydn’s humour is in the timing.

threads.title: Gravity
threads.body: Between the jokes, the Largo is the quartet’s serious centre, and the finale’s sudden Adagio borrows its solemn tone for a moment before the punchline.
